stem.text: A function h satisfies \( \lim_{x \to -\infty} h(x) = \frac{5}{2} \). Describe in words what this statement says about h and about its graph.

answer_key.label: As x decreases without bound, h(x) approaches \( \frac{5}{2} \), so the line \( y = \frac{5}{2} \) is a horizontal asymptote.

worked_solution.text: The input decreases without bound, so the statement is about the left end of the graph only.
The outputs approach the number \( \frac{5}{2} \) there, so the graph has the horizontal asymptote \( y = \frac{5}{2} \) at that end.
worked_solution.rule_named: limit at infinity and horizontal asymptote

options.label: As x decreases without bound, h(x) approaches \( \frac{5}{2} \), so the line \( y = \frac{5}{2} \) is a horizontal asymptote.
As x approaches \( \frac{5}{2} \), h(x) decreases without bound, so the line \( x = \frac{5}{2} \) is a vertical asymptote.
options.derivation: the limit at infinity read as an infinite limit at an input, with the roles of input and output exchanged

options.label: The value of h at the input \( -\infty \) is \( \frac{5}{2} \), so the graph of h contains the point \( (-\infty, \frac{5}{2}) \).
options.derivation: infinity treated as an input at which the function takes the value

options.label: As x increases or decreases without bound, h(x) approaches \( \frac{5}{2} \), so the line \( y = \frac{5}{2} \) is a horizontal asymptote at both ends.
options.derivation: the statement about one end read as describing both ends of the graph
